items.title: Associations of cumulative exposure, variability, and longitudinal profiles of CHG index with incident myocardial infarction among community-dwelling Chinese adults: a longitudinal analysis.
items.abstract: The cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and glucose (CHG) has been proposed as a composite metabolic index that may reflect disturbances in glucose and lipid metabolism associated with insulin resistance. We aimed to systematically evaluate the individual and joint associations of long-term patterns of the CHG index, including cumulative exposure, variability, and longitudinal profiles, with the risk of incident myocardial infarction (MI) among community-dwelling Chinese adults. This prospective cohort study included 72,312 participants from the Kailuan Study who completed three consecutive health examinations between 2006 and 2015. Multiple indicators were derived to characterize long-term patterns of the CHG index, including time-weighted cumulative CHG (TW-cumCHG), cumulative CHG burden, duration of elevated CHG, visit-to-visit CHG variability (CHGV), and longitudinal CHG profiles. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident MI. Discriminative performance was evaluated using the 10-year time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). During a median follow-up of 11.61 years, 2818 incident MI events were documented. After multivariable adjustment, the HR for incident MI was 2.17 (95% CI, 1.91-2.48) for participants in the highest quartile of TW-cumCHG, 1.64 (95% CI, 1.50-1.79) for those with a cumulative CHG burden >0, and 2.13 (95% CI, 1.87-2.41) for those with 6 years of elevated CHG exposure. Greater visit-to-visit CHGV and persistently high longitudinal CHG profiles were also associated with a higher risk of MI. Participants with both high TW-cumCHG and high CHGV had the greatest risk. Long-term CHG patterns provided modest incremental discrimination for incident MI beyond traditional risk factors and the individual CHG components, including FBG, TC, and HDL-C. Long-term patterns of the CHG index were associated with the risk of incident MI, potentially reflecting cumulative glucose-lipid exposure and metabolic instability. These findings highlight the significance of long-term CHG assessment and its potential to provide modest incremental information for early MI risk stratification beyond traditional risk factors.

items.title: Cumulative remnant cholesterol-adiposity product indices and incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective CHARLS analysis.
items.abstract: Remnant cholesterol (RC) and excess adiposity are jointly implicated in cardiometabolic disease, but whether their repeated joint burden adds information beyond a single measurement remains uncertain. We examined associations of cumulative RC-adiposity product indices and two-wave exposure patterns with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM). We included 5458 adults aged ≥45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study who were free of CMM in both 2011 and 2015. RC was multiplied by 11 adiposity indices at Wave 1 (2011-2012) and Wave 3 (2015) to derive time-weighted cumulative indices. CMM was defined as at least two of diabetes mellitus, heart disease, and stroke by 2020. Among 567 incident cases, higher cumulative RC-body mass index (RC-BMI), RC-body roundness index (RC-BRI), and RC-Chinese visceral adiposity index (RC-CVAI) were associated with higher odds after multivariable adjustment (per-1-SD odds ratios 1.167 [95% CI, 1.077-1.264], 1.188 [1.095-1.287], and 1.165 [1.076-1.260]; highest-versus lowest-quartile odds ratios 2.266, 2.322, and 2.292). The prioritized indices modestly improved discrimination over covariates alone (ΔAUC 0.004-0.007; DeLong P ≤ 0.033), and formal comparisons against component and interaction models supported their interpretation as pragmatic markers of joint remnant-adiposity burden rather than as synergistic constructs. Exploratory analyses suggested that hsCRP mediated a modest proportion of these associations (indirect proportions, 16.6%-21.3%). Sustained exposure and adverse two-wave patterns of RC-adiposity composite indices, particularly those reflecting central or visceral adiposity, were associated with incident CMM and may complement conventional risk stratification.

items.title: Associations of Plasma Branched-Chain Amino Acids With Incident Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease by Sex and Type 2 Diabetes Status Among Chinese Adults.
items.abstract: Evidence on associations between branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains limited, particularly in Chinese populations. We investigated associations between BCAAs and ASCVD and whether they differed by sex and Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Using a case-cohort design within a Chinese prospective cohort, we included a random subcohort (n = 2163) and incident ASCVD cases (n = 674). Plasma BCAA concentrations were quantified by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations of BCAAs with incident ASCVD were evaluated using Prentice-weighted Cox proportional hazards models, with stratified analyses and interaction tests by sex and T2D. Mediation analyses assessed the contribution of BCAAs to associations between T2D and ASCVD. During a median follow-up of 10.3 years, plasma BCAAs were positively associated with ASCVD. Associations appeared more pronounced among female participants, although interaction tests by sex were not statistically significant. Among female participants, significant associations were only observed in those with T2D, with hazard ratios (95% CIs) of 2.014 (1.185-3.423), 1.867 (1.142-3.052), 1.814 (1.071-3.078) and 2.030 (1.197-3.442) per standard deviation increment in ln-transformed total BCAA, isoleucine, leucine and valine, respectively. Additive interactions with T2D were detected for total BCAA and leucine. For male participants, no significant associations were observed, regardless of T2D status. Notably, total BCAA, leucine and valine partially mediated the association between T2D and ASCVD among female participants, with mediated proportions of 7.89%, 7.68% and 6.76%, respectively. Higher plasma BCAA concentrations were associated with increased incident ASCVD risk, supporting their potential role as metabolic markers of ASCVD.

items.title: Circadian clock adjusted classes improve sleep, circadian health, and academic performance in medical freshmen.
items.abstract: University students often experience circadian misalignment with academic schedules, which may impair performance. This study evaluated whether a later-start schedule improves academic outcomes and circadian rhythms in first-year medical students. Incoming students ( n = 220) completed the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire; those with high social jetlag (SJL >120 min, n = 71) were randomized into either a later-start schedule (LS; classes ≥10:00 a.m., n = 30) or a standard early-start schedule (ES; 8:00 a.m., n = 41). Actigraphy data were collected from 112 students prior to examinations. Based on the objective temperature circadian phase (TCP) with a median acrophase split at 3:59 a.m. ES participants were categorized asearly (ETCP-ES, n = 41) or late (LTCP-ES, n = 41). All LS participants exhibited a TCP later than 3:59 a.m. and remained LTCP-LS group ( n = 30). Associations between scheduling, circadian metrics, and exam scores were analyzed using regression and sex-adjusted ANCOVA. TCP predicted exam scores overall (β = -0.217, p = 0.021), most evidently within ES (β = -0.291, p = 0.008). LTCP-ES students scored lower than ETCP-ES students ( p = 0.025). LTCP-LS students performed similarly to ETCP-ES students and showed greater circadian robustness, including higher rest-activity stability (p = 0.031), greater blue-light stability ( p = 0.029), and longer sleep duration ( p = 0.013).

items.title: Interleukin 4-receptor-α blockade in localised scleroderma: a phase 2 proof-of-concept study.
items.abstract: Fibrotic diseases are a major therapeutic challenge. In humans, fibrosing diseases are often associated with an interleukin (IL-) 4/T H 2 signature. In preclinical mouse models, development of fibrosis critically depends on IL-4/signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6). Yet, the role of IL-4/IL-13 in human fibrosing diseases remains unknown, and treatment development requires a deeper understanding of the role of IL-4/IL-13 in the pathogenesis. The local inflammation and the development of fibrosis in localised scleroderma (LS) are similar to those in systemic sclerosis and other fibrosing diseases. In this article, we investigated the role of IL-4/IL-13 signalling in LS in a randomised, placebo-controlled clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT04200755). We studied the effect of 6 months of blocking IL-4-receptor α with dupilumab on disease progression, sclerosis-associated inflammation, and sclerosis-specific gene expression. Already this short-term intervention resulted in a significant clinical improvement over placebo, a significant attenuation of the local inflammation, a specific and significant reduction of the IL-4/IL-13-dependent gene signature, and a partial suppression of genes coding for fibrosis-inducing proteins. Thus, selective inhibition of IL-4/IL-13 prevents the progression of LS and is promising for therapeutic prevention of other fibrosing diseases.

items.title: Multilayered mechanisms driving sexual dimorphism in antitumor immunity.
items.abstract: Biological sex is a major variable associated with cancer incidence and treatment response, but how it affects antitumor immunity is not well understood. This review highlights the multilayered mechanisms driving sex differences in antitumor immunity. At the molecular level, tumor suppressor and oncogene alterations can be sex-biased and lead to the activation of noncanonical, immune-altering pathways. At the tissue level, resident immune niches and the commensal microbiome modulate sex-biased inflammation. Finally, at the organismal level, sex hormones and chromosomes, which act systemically across tissues, drive divergent inflammatory responses. Together, these mechanisms drive sex-specific antitumor responses, including differences in immunotherapy efficacy and toxicity. Further elucidating these mechanisms will advance precision oncology through sex-stratified treatment strategies and improve preclinical and clinical study designs.

items.title: Glutamine metabolic interaction network reshapes tumor immunotherapy resistance.
items.abstract: Glutamine metabolism is often viewed as a cancer cell dependency, but its biological consequences depend on how glutamine and its carbon- and nitrogen-derived metabolites are used across malignant, immune, and stromal compartments. In this article, we introduce the glutamine metabolic interaction network (GMIN) as an analytical framework that integrates nutrient partitioning, competition, metabolic cooperation, and metabolite-mediated regulation while distinguishing candidate associations from functionally supported interactions. We review the biochemical, spatial, and treatment-dependent determinants of GMIN states, including emerging evidence for metabolic remodeling during immunotherapy resistance. Current clinical evidence neither supports uniform glutaminase 1 dependence nor establishes a single preferred strategy for glutamine-directed intervention. GMIN may therefore provide a framework for identifying context-specific glutamine-centered interactions and prioritizing them for state-resolved therapeutic targeting.

items.title: History of Smoking and Prognosis of Patients With Non-small Cell Lung Cancer.
items.abstract: Smoking is a known risk factor for the development of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, conflicting results are reported in the literature regarding the risk of smoking on the prognosis of patients with NSCLC. Moreover, these studies were often conducted before the era of personalized targeted therapy and immunotherapy, which can significantly improve the prognosis of patients. The aim of the present study was to evaluate the prognosis of patients with NSCLC in relation to their smoking history. This retrospective multicentre study included all patients from the Czech LUCAS registry with baseline tumour characteristics. Overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier estimates, with differences between groups evaluated by the log-rank test and multivariate Cox regression model, adjusting for covariates and stratifying by disease stage when proportional hazards assumptions were violated. A total of 3,372 patients were included. In the univariate model, non-smokers had a significantly better prognosis than former and current heavy smokers (with a history of ≥40 pack-years), hazard ratio=1.19 (95% confidence interval=1.01-1.42), p =0.043; and hazard ratio 1.19 (95% confidence interval=0.03-1.37), p =0.018, respectively. This relationship was not significant in the multivariate model. The absence of a prognostic significance of smoking at the time of NSCLC diagnosis was also demonstrated in a multivariate model both in patients with advanced disease treated with anticancer drugs and in patients who underwent surgery. Although smoking/ex-smoking at the time of NSCLC diagnosis had a negative prognostic impact in univariate analysis, multivariate analysis did not demonstrate smoking itself as an independent prognostic factor for NSCLC. Therefore, other factors, including poorer performance status, likely contributed to the poorer outcome for smokers.

items.title: Locus-Specific Endogenous Retroviral Transcriptional Modulation in Viral Hepatitis-Driven Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) are remnants of ancient infections integrated into the primate germ line. HERV transcriptional reactivation has been observed in several diseases, including cancer, where it may reflect epigenetic deregulation, cellular stress, inflammation, and infections. Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most diffuse and deadly cancers worldwide, with chronic hepatitis infections as major etiological factors. In this context, the activation of specific HERV loci in HCC and their relationship with the broader tumor-associated transcriptional landscape remain poorly defined. Here, we characterized the expression of ∼3,300 HERVs in a public RNA-seq dataset comprising HCC samples, predominantly of viral etiology, and non-HCC liver controls. We identified 185 differentially expressed HERVs, predominantly upregulated in HCC (n=145): comparisons with GTEx healthy liver transcriptomes, inflammatory gene profiling, and covariate-adjusted analyses supported the consistency of this HCC-associated transcriptional signature. Aggregate expression scores of upregulated and downregulated HERVs showed significant associations with histological grade, with opposite trends across G1-G3 tumors. 16 HERV loci were consistently upregulated in all tumor tissues, and their aggregate expression increased significantly with histological grade, supporting their prioritization as a candidate HCC-associated signature. HERV-correlated pathway analyses revealed grade-associated patterns involving metabolic, inflammatory, interferon-related, and proliferative transcriptional programs. De novo transcript reconstruction identified candidate HERV-derived transcripts requiring experimental validation. Overall, the study provides a comprehensive characterization of HERV modulation in a predominantly viral-associated HCC cohort and identifies conserved HERV signatures embedded within the broader transcriptomic remodeling, for future independent and functional studies of their potential relevance to liver cancer biology.

items.title: Persistent Hepatocyte Plasticity and Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming After Hepatitis C Virus Cure.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection disrupts hepatocyte polarity and promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), contributing to liver disease progression. Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) eradicate HCV infection in most patients, the risk of fibrosis progression and hepatocellular carcinoma persists after viral clearance. Whether antiviral cure fully restores hepatocyte differentiation, polarity, and epithelial identity programs remains unclear. We investigated whether HCV-induced EMT and lipid metabolism alterations are fully reversible following DAA treatment. Huh7 hepatoma cells and Huh7 cells stably expressing a full-length HCV replicon were cultured in three-dimensional Matrigel to assess morphogenesis, polarity-associated features, and EMT. Spheroid morphology, canalicular-like organization, EMT markers, and transcriptomic signatures were analyzed using microscopy, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, and microarray analysis. The effects of DAA treatment (sofosbuvir with or without velpatasvir) were evaluated in vitro. Publicly available transcriptomic data from liver biopsies collected before therapy and within five days after its completion, were analyzed. HCV replicon expression altered canalicular-like organization and induced actin-rich protrusions in 90% of Huh7-R spheroids. DAA treatment efficiently suppressed HCV replicon expression and partially restored epithelial morphology, reducing protrusions to 25%, without normalizing them to the control level (2.5%). EMT-associated changes, including reduced E-cadherin and increased N-cadherin expression, were only partially corrected by DAA treatment. Transcriptomic EMT scoring showed persistent mesenchymal features in DAA-treated cells and in patient biopsies collected at the end of treatment. In parallel, genes involved in lipid metabolism and hepatocyte differentiation remained dysregulated. These findings show incomplete restoration of epithelial organization after suppression of HCV replicon expression in vitro and incomplete normalization of selected transcriptional signatures at the end of DAA treatment in patient liver samples. They suggest that cellular plasticity and metabolic reprogramming may persist after treatment and contribute to long-term liver disease risk.

items.title: Structural characterization and hepatoprotective activities of polysaccharides from Campanumoea javanica Bl.
items.abstract: Campanumoea javanica Bl. is a traditional herb used in Southwestern China for its "Qi-invigorating" and immune-strengthening properties. An acidic pectic heteropolysaccharide, CJPC, was isolated from its roots by hot water extraction followed by DEAE Sepharose Fast Flow and Sephacryl S-200 HR chromatography. CJP-C had a weight-average molecular weight of 32.6 kDa and consisted mainly of galactose, galacturonic acid, arabinose, and rhamnose (molar ratio 2.53:1.86:1.03:1.00). Its backbone comprised a homogalacturonan (HG) domain of α-1,4-linked GalpA residues and an RG-I domain of alternating α-1,4-GalpA and α-1,2-Rhap residues, the latter branched at O-4 of rhamnose with β-1,4-galactan, β-1,6-galactan, and α-1,5-arabinan side chains. Crude CJP and purified CJP-C showed broadly comparable immunomodulatory and antioxidant activities in vitro. In a Con A-induced autoimmune hepatitis mouse model, CJP (1200 mg/kg) significantly reduced serum ALT/AST, alleviated hepatic necrosis and inflammation, restored SOD and GSH-Px activities, lowered MDA, and suppressed IL-6, IL-1β, IFN-γ, MIP-1α, and ICAM-1. CJP treatment was associated with reduced total STAT1 protein expression, while T-bet levels were unchanged and SOCS1, a direct STAT1 target, was downregulated. These findings indicate that CJP alleviates Con A-induced hepatic injury, an effect associated with reduced oxidative stress and suppression of inflammatory signaling involving the IFN-γ/STAT1 axis, supporting its potential as a functional food or adjunctive therapy pending further validation.

items.title: Label-Free Nucleic Acid Amplification in a Self-regulated All-Fiber Photothermal Microcavity.
items.abstract: Nucleic acid amplification commonly relies on fluorescent labels and electrically driven thermal control, limiting simplicity, scalability, and remote deployment. Here, we establish a label-free optical strategy based on amplification-associated refractive-index (RI) evolution within a confined optothermal microcavity. During amplification, the accumulation of nucleic acid products alters the composition and molecular polarizability of the reaction medium, contributing to a progressive increase in its effective RI. This bulk RI change is converted into interferometric phase accumulation under thermally stabilized conditions, enabling real-time optical readout without labels. We implement this strategy in a 0.94 nL fiber Fabry-Perot microcavity that integrates localized optothermal regulation and phase-sensitive interrogation within a single optical pathway. The confined geometry enables rapid optothermal heating, reaching a 1 °C temperature rise in 15 ms, nearly three orders of magnitude faster than conventional electrical heating. Using hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA as a model target, we achieve a detection limit of 5.24 copies/nL and quantitative agreement with fluorescence-based assays, while isothermal amplification reduces the total assay time by approximately 50% relative to commercial qPCR. Frequency-division multiplexing enables parallel multi-target analysis, while stable transmission is maintained over 20 km fiber links. Our results establish amplification-associated RI evolution as a promising label-free transduction mechanism for fiber-integrated molecular diagnostics.

items.title: Community Health Worker Interventions Addressing Social Determinants of Health in Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Chronic diseases disproportionately affect people facing social and economic adversity. Community health workers (CHWs) are increasingly recognized as a key workforce for addressing social determinants of health (SDOH). However, evidence for the effect of CHW-led interventions on social and clinical outcomes among US adults with chronic disease is limited. This systematic review evaluated the effects of CHW-led interventions on SDOH and health outcomes. Following PRISMA guidelines and a registered Prospero protocol, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and Embase (Ovid) in April 2024 for US-based randomized or quasi-experimental studies involving adults with chronic disease and a patient-facing CHW intervention addressing at least 1 SDOH domain. Eligible studies were required to have a comparator group and report social or health outcomes. We used standardized forms to extract data and assess quality. We identified 1,939 records and screened 1,058 abstracts. We reviewed 110 full-text articles; 7 studies met inclusion criteria. All were randomized controlled trials addressing at least 1 SDOH domain. Interventions most commonly targeted health care access, housing stability, or care coordination among adults with diabetes, HIV, asthma, hepatitis C, or hearing loss. CHW interventions demonstrated improvements in several condition-specific clinical outcomes, but overall effects on major clinical indicators were modest and inconsistent. CHW-led interventions show promise for addressing social needs and improving engagement in care among adults with chronic disease, but evidence of meaningful clinical benefit is still limited. The lack of large, well-powered trials underscores the need for more rigorous research to strengthen the evidence base for CHW-driven SDOH interventions in US health systems.

items.title: French prospective cohort study of predictors of fruquintinib efficacy in real-world metastatic colorectal cancer (PRODIGE 108 - COHORTE 2320 - COFRUQ).
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. In unresectable metastatic (m)CRC, systemic therapy is the standard of care, and maintaining anti-angiogenic pressure remains important in the chemorefractory setting, as shown in 2nd and 3rd line treatment. Fruquintinib, a selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor of VEGF receptors 1, 2, and 3, recently demonstrated a 2.6-month overall survival benefit versus placebo in advanced mCRC and is now a new option for heavily pre-treated patients. However, real-world data on fruquintinib use and predictors of its efficacy remain limited. PRODIGE108-COHORTE2320 - COFRUQ (NCT07124858) is a French multicentre prospective observational cohort primarily designed to identify clinical and biological factors associated with fruquintinib efficacy under real-world conditions. The primary endpoint is investigator-assessed overall survival. Main secondary objectives include progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, safety, and quality of life. Eligible patients are ≥18 years old with histologically confirmed mCRC receiving fruquintinib within its EMA indication. Biological studies (tumour and blood collection) will identify prognostic and predictive biomarkers, alongside pharmacokinetic analyses. The cohort aims to enrol 300 patients over 3 years and has been open for enrolment in France since March 2026.

items.title: Co-delivery of Sorafenib and Anti-miR-21 via a CD44-guided Nanocarrier for Dual-pathway Inhibition in HCC Cells.
items.abstract: The clinical efficacy of sorafenib against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is severely limited by limited efficacy and off-target toxicity. Overexpression of oncogenic miR-21 has been identified as a key driver of these limitations, as it downregulates the tumor suppressors PTEN and PDCD4, thereby aberrantly activating both the PI3K/Akt and STAT3 signaling pathways. To address the limitations of conventional sorafenib therapy, we aimed to construct a smart nanocarrier capable of simultaneously delivering sorafenib (SF) and anti-miR-21 specifically to HCC cells. We designed a core-shell nanoparticle consisting of a PAMAM dendrimer/anti-miR-21 polyplex core and a hyaluronic acid-sorafenib conjugate shell. This architecture enables CD44-mediated active targeting and pH-responsive drug release in the acidic tumor microenvironment. The antitumor activity of the co-delivery system was evaluated in vitro using HepG2 cells, with assessments of cell proliferation, migration, apoptosis, and the underlying signaling pathways. The prepared nanoparticle exhibited potent anti-proliferative, anti-migratory, and pro-apoptotic effects in HepG2 cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that these benefits were associated with the reduced phosphorylation of key proteins in both the PI3K/Akt/mTOR and STAT3 cascades, effectively counteracting the therapy limitations that are normally fueled by miR-21 overexpression. Our findings demonstrate that CD44-guided co-delivery of sorafenib and anti-miR-21 provides a promising nanotherapeutic strategy to counteract therapy limitations through coordinated blockade of two major oncogenic pathways in HCC cells.

items.title: Patterns of Progression on Posttreatment Imaging During [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
items.abstract: We characterized patterns of treatment response and progression during [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) using serial posttreatment SPECT/CT and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET imaging and evaluated cycle-by-cycle prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-imaging concordance. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 361 patients from 2 academic centers who received at least 2 cycles of [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT between May 2017 and March 2025. Posttreatment SPECT/CT scans were qualitatively evaluated to determine the site and pattern of response and progression, including PSMA low-avidity and PSMA-negative disease. Progression was defined by the appearance of new lesions or at least a 2-fold growth in preexisting lesions on SPECT/CT. PSA response was defined per Prostate Cancer Clinical Trials Working Group 3 criteria as at least a 50% decline from baseline. For cycle-by-cycle concordance analysis, PSA change was classified directionally as rising or falling relative to the prior cycle. In patients who paused or completed RPT after response, progression imaging was compared with the final on-treatment SPECT/CT scan. Results: Overall, 290 of 361 (80%) patients demonstrated a decrease in lesion size or number on posttreatment imaging. Of 312 patients with baseline bone disease, 81% demonstrated a response on posttreatment imaging. In total, 156 of 361 patients (43%) demonstrated progression during treatment. New osseous lesions developed in 132 patients, of whom 89 (67%) had PSMA low-avidity disease. At cycle 2, 64% of new lesions were osseous, increasing to at least 90% by cycles 4-6. PSMA-negative progression occurred in 22 patients (6%), predominantly in the liver ( n = 11) and lymph nodes ( n = 8), with 59% detected at cycle 2. Among 81 patients with imaging available at PSA progression after treatment completion or pause, 74 (91%) had imaging progression; of these, 69 (93%) demonstrated osseous and 13 (18%) nodal progression. PSA and imaging were discordant in 25%-43% of patients across cycles, with discordance increasing from cycle 2 to cycle 6. Conclusion: Progression during [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT occurs most frequently in bone, with 67% of patients with new osseous lesions demonstrating a PSMA low-avidity disease component. PSMA-negative progression is uncommon and tends to emerge early. PSA-imaging discordance is frequent, underscoring the need for integrated imaging assessment throughout treatment.
